about: Every number the model uses that is not a market price, with the document it was read in. Dated tables apply from the date given until the next row.

mmbtu_per_mwh.source: NIST Special Publication 811, appendix B.9: one Btu (International Table) is 1,055.05585262 J

mmbtu_per_m3_lng.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.8, page 2, 'LNG Conversion Factor: 23'; 22 to 24 covers lean to rich cargoes

mmbtu_per_tonne_lng.source: IEA and Eurostat, Energy Statistics Manual, 2004, Annex 3, Table A3.9: LNG, 51,560 Btu per kilogramme, gross

knots_to_nm_per_day.source: one knot is one nautical mile an hour

ships.name: 160,000 m3 TFDE
ships.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.2 (11 November 2022), page 2: 'Vessel Type: 160,000 m3 TFDE', 'Boil Off Rate: 0.1% of cargo tanks at 98.5% capacity'; GTT's Mark III Flex 'reduces the boil-off rate from 0.15% to 0.10% of the cargo volume per day' (gCaptain, 10 October 2012)

ships.name: 174,000 m3 two-stroke
ships.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.8, page 2: 'Vessel Type: 174,000 m3 2 Stroke', 'Boil Off Rate: 0.085% of cargo tanks at 98.5% capacity'; change log, version 3.5 of 2 January 2024, 'Vessel Type updated to 174,000 m3 2 Stroke'; GTT's NO96 Super+ 'offers a guaranteed boil-off rate of 0,085%V/d' for a 174,000 m3 carrier (LNG Prime, 16 April 2021)

fill.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology: boil-off and discharge volume are stated on '98.5% of Vessel Capacity'

speed_kn.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.8, page 2, 'Speed: 17 knots'

load_days.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.8, page 2, '1 day load'

discharge_days.source: Spark LNG Freight Methodology 3.8, page 2, '1 day discharge'

canal_days_per_transit.source: This study. The Panama Canal Authority's monthly summaries put the average time in canal waters, waiting included, at 20 to 38 hours in 2026 (20.2 hours in October 2026); a Suez transit takes about half a day in convoy

europe_usd.source: Spark Commodities, note on negative freight rates, February 2022: Sabine Pass and Gate together, 'Port costs provided by GAC on an indicative basis', for a 160,000 m3 TFDE. Held for every year and both ships

asia_usd.source: Spark Commodities, the same note: 'Port Cost' for Sabine Pass to Futtsu via Panama on its Routes page, release of 8 February 2022. Held for every route east, every year and both ships

tolls.source: Panama Canal Authority, tolls approved for 1 April 2016; Tolls Assessment, May 2023, page 11
Panama Canal Authority, tolls approved 1 August 2017; Tolls Assessment, May 2023, page 21
Panama Canal Authority, Tolls, September 2020, page 26
Panama Canal Authority, tariff items 1010.FN02, 1010.NN01 and 1010.BA01, 1 January 2023
Panama Canal Authority, tariff item 1010, 1 January 2024
Panama Canal Authority, tariff item 1010, 1 January 2025: 1010.FN02 300,000 USD a transit, 1010.NN01 2.05 USD per m3, 1010.BA01 ballast at 85 percent; unchanged in the tariff list of 15 October 2026

fresh_water.source: Panama Canal Authority, tariff item 1500.RWA2: 10,000 USD a transit for ships over 300 feet; the variable part runs from 0 to 10 percent of the toll with the level of Gatun Lake (advisories A-03-2020 and A-42-2023), taken here at 5 percent

booking_fee.source: Panama Canal Authority, neopanamax booking fee at the opening of the expanded locks
Panama Canal Authority, booking fee for a beam of 42.67 m or more, booking dates from 1 June 2021
Panama Canal Authority, tariff list of January 2024
Panama Canal Authority, tariff item 1050.IBN1, 1 January 2025; unchanged in the tariff list of 15 October 2026

waits_reported.source: Spark, in LNG Prime, 28 July 2023: 12 days of delay for unbooked vessels
EIA, Today in Energy, 31 October 2023: neopanamax ships 'had to wait at least 17 days' in August 2023
IEA, Gas Market Report Q1 2024: about 15 days for unreserved slots in mid December 2023

scnt_per_m3.source: A canal agency's approximation, 'ca 85.000 SCNT (145.000m3)' for a membrane LNG carrier, scaled to the capacity

dues_sdr_per_scnt.source: Suez Canal Authority, transit dues from 1 May 2015, LNG row unchanged in the schedules of 2020 and 2022
Suez Canal Authority, circular 14/2022 of 18 September 2022
Suez Canal Authority, circular 7/2023 of 16 October 2023

lng_surcharge.source: Suez Canal Authority, periodical 20/2026 of 7 June 2026

general_lng_reduction.source: periodical of 14 March 2022, the reduction cancelled

us_gulf_to_asia_rebate.source: periodical of 21 June 2023, renewed every six months to 31 December 2026 (periodical 8/2026)

suez.rule: toll = normal dues by band x (1 + surcharge - the larger of the route rebate and the general reduction), in SDR, at the day's dollars per SDR

route_status.note: The expanded locks open on 26 June 2016; the old locks are too small for the ship
route_status.source: Panama Canal Authority, press release of 26 June 2016

route_status.note: First LNG carrier through the expanded locks on 25 July 2016, from Sabine Pass
route_status.source: Panama Canal Authority, press release of 25 July 2016

route_status.note: Drought: daily transits cut to 32 and booking slots to 24 by January 2024; unbooked LNG carriers reported waiting 12 to 17 days; LNG transits fall from 326 in fiscal 2023 to 115 in fiscal 2024
route_status.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisories A-35-2023, A-48-2023 and A-54-2023

route_status.note: Normal operating conditions again, 36 booking slots a day, 10 of them neopanamax. Slots are sold by booking, auction and long-term allocation; LNG use stays low (61 transits in fiscal 2025). On 9 November 2026: 34 slots a day, 10 neopanamax, draught back to 50 feet
route_status.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisories A-28-2024 and A-42-2026

route_status.note: Routine use: 130 US cargoes went south through the canal in 2023
route_status.source: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, NG 188, February 2024

route_status.note: Red Sea: the last laden LNG carrier passed on 12 January 2024. Since then a handful of crossings a year, none reported for a US cargo to Asia; a Qatari cargo to Europe in October 2026 was reported as rare
route_status.source: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, NG 188; gCaptain, October 2026

ets.source: Directive 2003/87/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/959: Article 3ga, half of the emissions of a voyage between an EU port and a port outside the EU and all emissions at berth in the EU; Article 3gb, 40 percent of 2024 emissions surrendered, 70 percent of 2025, all from 2026; Annex I, methane and nitrous oxide from 1 January 2026. Emission factors and default methane slip (Otto dual fuel, slow speed 1.7 percent, medium speed 3.1 percent): Regulation (EU) 2015/757, Annex I, as replaced by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2776. Warming potentials: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1044

henry_hub_multiple.source: Sabine Pass Liquefaction and Centrica, LNG sale and purchase agreement of 22 March 2013, section 9.1.1: 'CSP = (1.15 x HH) + X'

liquefaction_fee_usd_mmbtu.source: The fixed fee most Sabine Pass contracts carry (Cheniere Energy Partners, Form 10-K for 2015, pages 9 and 88); 2.25 for BG's first volumes, 3.50 in the Corpus Christi contract with Woodside

cancellation_notice.value: the 20th of the month two months before loading

spread.source: This study: 150 basis points over SOFR, a trading house's short-term borrowing

day_count.source: The money market convention SOFR is quoted on

finance.financed: 115 percent of Henry Hub on the cargo loaded, from loading to discharge

window_days.source: This study: the mean of the last 20 daily values ACER published, because a single day mixes an assessment struck during the day with a futures settlement

before_acer_eur_mwh.source: ACER, Gas market trends and price drivers, October 2023, page 13: 'the average price difference between TTF front-month products and the EU LNG spot reference price was 2 EUR/MWh in 2023 (1 January to 31 August 2023)'

squeeze_2022.source: ACER, European LNG market developments, April 2024, paragraph 83: the spread 'exceeded 35 EUR/MWh during most days from end-July to mid-October 2022', when terminals and pipelines into Northwest Europe were congested

hire.note: Low, central and high are the quartiles of the rates reported for the ship in use, rounded to 250 USD a day as Spark quotes them. Zero is the sunk case: tonnage already on term charter.

flows.rule: Fixed before the result was computed: a month is open when its mean JKM minus TTF is above the breakeven of the cheapest open route at the reported charter rate; its verdict is set against the share of the cargoes that left the following month.

spark_example.source: Spark Commodities, note on negative freight rates, February 2022, assessment of 8 February 2022, Sabine Pass to Gate and back on a 160,000 m3 TFDE

platts_arbitrage_2026_04_28.source: Platts, republished by Cyprus Shipping News, 5 May 2026: US arbitrage to North Asia against the Atlantic

cancellations_2020.source: EIA, Today in Energy, 11 August 2020: cargoes cancelled, EIA's estimate for June and July, trade press reports for August and September

cape_use_2024_03.source: Platts, republished by Hellenic Shipping News, 22 April 2024: a record 27 US cargoes to Asia via the Cape of Good Hope in March 2024, against one via Panama
